question.problem: Given the hyperboloid of two sheets $(x+1)^{2}+(y-2)^{2}-\frac{{z}^{2}}{9}=-1,$ find the domain of $z=z(x,y).$
question.worked_solution:
From the hyperboloid equation, we make $z$ the subject as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}(x+1)^{2}+(y-2)^{2}-\frac{{z}^{2}}{9} & =-1 \\ (x+1)^{2}+(y-2)^{2}+1 & =\frac{{z}^{2}}{9}\end{aligned}
$$

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{{z}^{2}}{9} & =(x+1)^{2}+(y-2)^{2}+1 \\ {z}^{2} & =9((x+1)^{2}+(y-2)^{2}+1) \\ z & =\pm 3\sqrt{(x+1)^{2}+(y-2)^{2}+1}\end{aligned}
$$

The square root is defined only for non-negative arguments. However, notice that for all $(x,y)\in {R}^{2},$ we have

$$
(x+1)^{2}+(y-2)^{2}+1\ge 0.
$$

Therefore, the domain of $z(x,y)$ is ${R}^{2}.$
